Subject: Clarify IP & cross-border handling for POC – AvaTech

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our data protection team returned a couple of questions after reviewing the draft DPA and the security pack. We need clear answers on two items before we can move to procurement:

1) Prompt/response ownership: we want confirmation that prompts and model responses generated during the POC will be treated as our customer content (no transfer of IP to Redwood) and that Redwood will not use them to improve models unless we opt in.

2) Cross-border export paths / subprocessors: we need a short list of the likely transfer mechanisms if we request SFTP export vs API export, and evidence that subprocessor access is limited to the redacted KV/cache and audit logs only.

I attached the redlined DPA for reference — you can send legal or ops contact details for evidence. Can we get a written note for procurement by EOD Wednesday PST?

Appreciate it,
Amanda Li
Corporate Counsel | AvaTech Inc.

Amanda — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (legal), Dev (prod infra) and Neha (privacy ops) so we can give you precise language and a short evidence bundle. High-level answers:

- Prompt/response IP: Redwood treats customer prompts and responses as customer data. We will not assert ownership of customer-generated content; customers retain their rights.
- Model improvement: By default our hosted offering uses aggregated telemetry only; we can commit to a customer-scoped "no-improvement" flag for the POC that prevents retention for training. We will provide the opt-out statement you can insert into the DPA.
- Exports & subprocessors: Exports can be delivered via API or SFTP. SFTP export will land in a customer-controlled sftp target (your endpoint). If we provide an on-prem or VPC deployment, data never leaves the customer environment. Subprocessor inventory attached — the folks with access to export mechanics are limited to our infra ops team and require joint approval.

We should follow up with a short email from Legal with proposed DPA language and an ops note that lists the specific export workflows + minimal audit logs we can share. Targeting EOD Wednesday (8/11).

—Jordan
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Hi Amanda — following up with explicit language you can drop into the DPA and a short evidence list. Please find proposed snippets below (we can iterate):

1) No-learning / model improvement opt-out (POC):
"Redwood Inference will not use Customer Data (including prompts and generated responses) to improve, train, or update any model used to provide the Services for the duration of the POC unless Customer provides explicit, written consent. Redwood will implement a technical no-improvement flag that prevents retention of model-level telemetry and prompt/response content for training workflows."

2) Prompt/response ownership:
"Customer retains all rights, title, and interest in Customer Data. Redwood does not claim ownership of prompts or generated outputs produced in response to Customer Data."

3) Export paths & evidence:
- API export: logs show per-request delivery status and server region (we can provide redacted example).
- SFTP export: data pushes originate from our IP ranges; audit trail includes transfer timestamps, file hashes, and delivery confirmation.
- Subprocessors: attached is a CSV inventory of subprocessors and their roles. Access to raw prompts/responses is restricted to the infra ops group; any access is logged and requires an incident-style approval ticket.

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory_aug2027.csv; audit_evidence_export_paths.txt (sample log snippets).

If this language looks fine, I can prepare a short cover note for procurement and include the two sample logs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Amanda, quick ops note to clarify technical controls referenced by Marissa:

- No-improvement flag: implemented as a request header / tenant config that disables persistent storage of prompt/response payloads to our model-training pipeline. When set, ephemeral KV caching is still used for inference latency but cache entries are deleted according to the POC retention schedule (configurable, default 7 days).

- Export workflows:
  * API export: customer calls our export endpoint; transfers are TLS 1.3 to your endpoint, with region header (we can include us-west/us-east).
  * Push to SFTP: we connect from a fixed outbound IP range (listed in the subprocessor CSV) and perform PGP-signed uploads.

- Evidence bundle we can share: sample API delivery log (redacted), SFTP transfer log with IP & hash, and a screenshot of the no-improvement tenant toggle in the console.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute runbook demo (ops) to show the export and the audit logs.

—Dev
